newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's ruling party begins election assembly.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's ruling party begins election assembly.

text.p: Malaysia's ruling party on Wednesday opened its triennial election assembly, a showcase for the party's rising and falling stars, analysts say.
Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim opened the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) general assembly with an address to its women and youth wings.
"UMNO Youth and Wanita UMNO (the women's wing) are not only pillars of UMNO but historically...the frontline and bulwark of the party," Anwar said.
Elections for leadership positions in the youth and women wings take place on Wednesday. Polls for other party positions will be held on Thursday.
UMNO is the main party in the ruling National Front coalition, which has governed Malaysia since independence from Britain in 1957.

Political analysts say the UMNO polls are more significant than general elections, which the National Front has always won easily. By political convention, UMNO's president and deputy president become prime minister and deputy prime minister.
Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad and Anwar are unchallenged for the top two jobs in UMNO under a pact made at last year's convention.
But 185 candidates are contesting other positions, including three vice presidencies, 30 seats on the policy-making Supreme Council, and heads of the youth and women wings of the party.
Political analysts tend to view the contests as a kind of proxy battle between the 70-year-old Mahathir and his ambitious and charismatic 49-year-old deputy.
Mahathir was given a significant boost on Tuesday after a Malay splinter party, led by his old political rival and former finance minister Tengku Razaleigh Hamzah, rejoined UMNO.
The 200,000 members of the defunct Spirit of '46 swelled UMNO's total membership to 2.5 million, party officials said.
UMNO has decreed a total ban on campaigning for the party posts, which in previous years has seen delegates selling votes to candidates all too willing to pay, party officials said.
Mahathir, in an informal speech to delegates on Tuesday, urged them to reject candidates who practised "money politics" or vote buying.
"UMNO does not want leaders who are corrupt, insincere and dirty," he said, adding he was prepared to risk his popularity in a crusade to stamp out corruption in the party.
On Monday, the party disqualified seven candidates from contesting the elections for campaign abuses.
